source.extraction: First HTML pre block; remove HTML tags, HTML-unescape once, UTF-8 encode; preserve leading and trailing whitespace.

differences: Both order count descending and encoded key ascending. YIAN insertion sort is used only for the at-most-16 one/two-base frequency rows; query outputs are not sorted.

Both roll two-bit keys for every complete window and update an actual hash table, materialize entries, sort, and emit the same nucleotide labels and three-decimal percentage through the standard library's `:.3f` specification. YIAN uses HashMap<u64,u32>; C uses khash with a custom XOR/shift hash.
Both build a map for each query length, encode the requested sequence, and perform a key lookup. YIAN constructs the encoded sequence in a growing Vec and outputs in the official query order.

C reads lines and grows a raw byte buffer; YIAN reads stdin in 8192-byte chunks and extracts the THREE sequence into encoded u8 values. Both stop at the next record and process lengths 1,2,3,4,6,12,18.

The official OpenMP pragmas are left in C source but are inactive because the task build does not use -fopenmp; YIAN executes serially. C and YIAN differ in map hashing/layout, bucket growth, allocation strategy, and materialization/sort implementation.

dependencies.name: klib khash.h
dependencies.note: Header-only dependency; original MIT notice retained; no binary library.
